chunk.text: When it comes to leaving at the top, I remember one more thing. If we talk about the first big issue in football this week, it is Mohamed Salah leaving Liverpool, friends. Everybody in the chat, I want you to describe Mohamed Salah in one word. Starting with Yash—you as well. Describe Mohamed Salah in one word, bro. On a very serious level, I would say one word: consistent. Consistent. Champion. Legend. Legend, bro. As a United fan, I would say nightmare. Nightmare, bro. That’s respect. If rival fans are happy when you leave the club, that’s respect. I’ll give you the floor—talk about Mohamed Salah and the respect he deserves.

I think at this time—and not just now, but in general—whenever a player leaves football, his value increases a lot. We saw this with Toni Kroos as well. Kroos performed at a very high level for many years, but when people realized he had one or two seasons left, especially his final season, they started appreciating his football even more. Every pass he used to make routinely suddenly became celebrated. As a United fan and a Premier League watcher, what has this guy done for the league? I won’t put filters when speaking as a rival.

Not at all. The biggest compliment I can give Mohamed Salah as a Liverpool player, being a United fan, is that I absolutely hated him. He made our lives miserable. He is among the top goal scorers at Old Trafford in the Premier League era—and he’s a rival player. Think about that impact. In his first five matches, he had zero goal contributions in this fixture, and after that, he peaked brilliantly. There’s always a debate—Salah vs Ronaldo, Salah vs Hazard—but forget that and just look at his impact.

Since his arrival at Liverpool, no other player outscored him. No one had more goal contributions or assists. He has been a top performer every single year. These are the stats since his debut. In terms of trophies, he has won everything with Liverpool: the Champions League, Premier League, Club World Cup, FA Cup, Carabao Cup, and UEFA Super Cup. If someone only watches him this season, they might think he’s declined, but you have to look at the bigger picture.

You have to look at where he came from and the impact he made at Liverpool. He was a Chelsea reject, then went to Fiorentina and Roma. When he came from Roma, people doubted whether he could adapt to the Premier League’s physicality. But then—44 goals in his first season, followed by 27, 23, 31—even during weaker Liverpool seasons, his numbers remained insane. The numbers speak for themselves.

Only one season where he had single-digit assists—that’s crazy. He was linked to Real Madrid at one point. Salah is not like Hazard, who focuses more on dribbling flair. He is more like a Ronaldo-type winger—goal-oriented. He has incredible durability too. Over 300 matches since 2017 with very few injuries—that is elite consistency. His goal ratio is insane.

Even if this season hasn’t been great, there is no doubt he is one of the best wingers in Premier League history. Not just a goal scorer—his assist numbers are also elite. In the final third, whenever he got the ball, something happened—either a goal, a shot, or a key chance. He always created output.

That is extremely important at the top level. Since 2000, he ranks among the top assist providers—around 93 assists. He is just below Thomas Muller in that list. Since 2017, in terms of total goal contributions in Europe, he ranks among the top players—alongside names like Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappe. That puts him in an elite category.

His impact at Liverpool is massive. They will truly realize how difficult it is to replace him. He didn’t join a peak Liverpool side—he joined during a rebuilding phase. The project was built around players like Mane and Salah. And to end it like this, with so many trophies, is a successful project.

He is a Ballon d’Or-level player. Last season stood out. Even after Klopp left, he remained elite. A player’s performance can change drastically under different coaches, but Salah maintained his level. Liverpool were competing for every trophy, and he was a major reason.

He was even a Ballon d’Or favorite until January. Eventually others stepped up, but his season was outstanding. Beyond goals and assists, his leadership is underrated. People talk about the front three—Mane, Firmino—but Salah’s contribution made Trent Alexander-Arnold’s role easier with his pressing and defensive work.
Liverpool now face a major challenge replacing him. They have signed players in attack but haven’t properly planned for Salah’s replacement. Finding someone with his output is extremely difficult.

If you had to pick a replacement in Europe, who would it be? Raphinha is somewhat similar. Earlier, Jarrod Bowen was a close comparison. Semenyo could also have been an option. Liverpool were reportedly interested in him.
Michael Olise is being mentioned, but he is more creative than goal-focused. Salah had pace, strength, and goal output. Very few players combine all those traits.
Rodrygo is not a direct replacement. He prefers central roles. If Liverpool wanted a right winger, he wouldn’t be the ideal choice for that role.
The closest profiles today are Olise, Yamal, and Raphinha. An outside shout could be Morgan Rogers. But realistically, replacing Salah is extremely difficult.
